description: The persistent storage contract of a device SDK (what the react package writes). Every value is a string. Replayed by the wrapper packages, not by the core suite: packages/react/__tests__/utils.test.ts asserts the same values. A port with its own storage MUST use these keys and serialisations so a user can upgrade from one SDK to another on the same device without losing the cache or the device id.
source: packages/react/utils.ts: storeKeys, translationsKeyFor(namespace), lastRefreshKeyFor(namespace), clearI18nKeylessStorage; packages/react/store.ts: hydrate()

lastRefresh.value: the delta cursor of the default namespace, raw string; set to the empty string on a language switch

translations.value: JSON object: the default namespace's dictionary for the current language

translationsUsage.value: JSON object keyed by namespace: { namespace: { storageKey: 'YYYY-MM-DD' } }; set to the empty string after a successful usage POST

namespaces.value: JSON array of the persisted namespaces (unpersisted ones excluded)

originNamespaces.value: JSON array of the namespaces that hold user-generated-content keys (unpersisted ones excluded)

hydrationOrder: i18n-keyless-user-id (device runtime only; an invalid or missing value is replaced by a fresh id, persisted at once); every outbound request is held until this step is done
i18n-keyless-namespaces, else ['default']; then for each namespace: its translations key, then its last-refresh key
i18n-keyless-translations-usage (a legacy flat map whose values are strings is discarded)
i18n-keyless-current-language (kept as stored; validated against `supported` by the language switch that follows)

adapterMethodResolution.notes: The first method present is used; sync or async. A failing read yields null and is logged. A failing write is logged and rethrown.

cases.name: namespace with a space is not encoded in the storage key
clear removes every key except the device id
